name: Vercel

@vercel/blob.detail: Cellar (S3 API) replaces Vercel Blob: server-side upload, delivery route, same keys
@vercel/blob.client: @aws-sdk/client-s3 with endpoint https://$CELLAR_ADDON_HOST, region us-east-1, forcePathStyle: true, credentials CELLAR_ADDON_KEY_ID / CELLAR_ADDON_KEY_SECRET, bucket $CELLAR_BUCKET

symbols.short: client-token upload (handleUpload) → server upload route: authenticate, check type/size on the bytes, PutObject to Cellar
symbols.what: the browser gets an upload token from this route and sends the file to Vercel: replace by a server route that authenticates the user first, receives the file (multipart/FormData), checks the real type and size on the bytes, and writes it with PutObject to Cellar (same key scheme); give PutObject a Buffer (await file.arrayBuffer()) or a ContentLength, never a stream of unknown length (fails with MissingContentLength); the SDK default checksums work on Cellar, no requestChecksumCalculation setting needed (verified 2026-10-25, @aws-sdk/client-s3 3.1156.0)

symbols.short: uploader → POST the file (FormData) to the new upload route
symbols.what: the uploader calls @vercel/blob/client upload(): POST the file as FormData to the new server upload route instead

symbols.short: delivery → GetObject from Cellar, stream with nosniff + CSP sandbox, inline only png/jpeg/webp/gif
symbols.what: the delivery route reads the blob: read it with GetObject from Cellar and stream it with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox; inline only for png/jpeg/webp/gif, otherwise attachment + application/octet-stream; authenticate first
server-side write: PutObject to Cellar with the same key (no random suffix unless the code relied on it)
listing or deletion: ListObjectsV2 / DeleteObject / CopyObject on Cellar

@vercel/blob.package_change: package.json: replace @vercel/blob by @aws-sdk/client-s3@3.1156.0 (latest stable on npm, published 2026-10-22, read 2026-10-25: re-check with npm view @aws-sdk/client-s3 version) and commit the lockfile
@vercel/blob.migration: existing blobs: list them with the Vercel token kept in a 600 file (never printed), then scripts/migrate-files.py --source <listing> --bucket <prefix>-files --create-bucket (keys kept, SHA-256 verified)

shared_client.short: new: one shared S3Client (endpoint https://$CELLAR_ADDON_HOST, region us-east-1, forcePathStyle, CELLAR_ADDON_KEY_ID/SECRET) + the bucket name, used by the routes
shared_client.what: create one module that builds the S3Client from CELLAR_ADDON_HOST / CELLAR_ADDON_KEY_ID / CELLAR_ADDON_KEY_SECRET (endpoint https://$CELLAR_ADDON_HOST, region us-east-1, forcePathStyle: true) and exports CELLAR_BUCKET; every route imports it

kept.vercel.json: ignored by Clever (harmless); delete it when you leave Vercel
kept.next_config_hosts: images host *.vercel-storage.com: harmless (files now come from the app's own route); remove after the migration

@vercel/blob.open_risk: OPEN RISK: the source has NO auth mechanism, so upload and delivery stay anonymous as on Vercel (kept, not fixed by this POC) — next step: an upload secret checked by the route, or an auth library

@vercel/kv.detail: Redis add-on with ioredis/redis (KV is a Redis REST wrapper)

@vercel/edge-config.detail: environment variables or a small table

@vercel/functions.detail: waitUntil/geolocation helpers: plain async code on a long-lived server

@vercel/otel.detail: OpenTelemetry works; point the exporter to your collector

crons.detail: clevercloud/cron.json + a job script; jobs run with an EMPTY environment: CC_PRE_RUN_HOOK writes the needed variables to a 600 file the job sources

traps: The runtime runs npm install but NOT the build: CC_POST_BUILD_HOOK="npm run build" (pnpm/yarn equivalent).
No NODE_ENV=production before the build: it drops devDependencies the build needs.
NEXT_PUBLIC_* / VITE_* are inlined at build: set them before the first build; prove them with prove.sh --asset-expect.
VERCEL_URL is undefined on Clever: use your own variable with the app's domain.
Next.js 16 renamed middleware.ts to proxy.ts: it runs inside next start, nothing to port.
A next build that is Killed needs a bigger build flavor (M by default here), not a bigger instance.

Cron jobs (clevercloud/cron.json) run with an EMPTY environment: no app variables, no INSTANCE_NUMBER, no PORT. CC_PRE_RUN_HOOK writes the needed ones to a 600 git-ignored file that the job script sources (see reference/runtimes-hooks.md).
Vercel Blob tokens (BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN) are secrets: keep them in a 600 file, never in chat, never on a command line.

All Vercel reads go through scripts/source-vercel.sh (names, one secret into a 600 file, blob listing): never run `vercel env ls` (prints truncated value prefixes) nor `vercel env pull` (writes ALL variables) yourself.
